name: St. Louis Marathon
summary: The St. Louis Marathon (earlier called the GO! St. Louis Marathon) is held in April. It starts downtown. A race listing says the course tours the Gateway Arch, Soulard, Tower Grove Park, Forest Park and other landmarks.
courseHighlights: Anheuser-Busch Brewery and Tower Grove Park
Finish festival outside CITYPARK next to Union Station

paceStrategy.summary: Race listings and a runner recap describe rolling hills, with frequent climbs in and after Forest Park. Run the early miles calmly and keep energy for the later hills.

segments.terrain: Downtown, Soulard and the Anheuser-Busch area, with a hill on Olive Street
segments.advice: Run controlled; a runner recap names a climb called Holy Hill around miles 6 to 8.

segments.terrain: Forest Park area, where a runner recap reports frequent hills
segments.advice: Run by effort and keep a steady rhythm.
Take fluids and fuel on time; the recap says hills continue after mile 22.

fuelingNotes: The race site does not list aid stations in the text I read; check the official course map. Take a gel before the Forest Park hills, around mile 7.
tips: The course is subject to change; check the interactive map on the official page
The marathon starts early on a Saturday morning
The finish festival is outside CITYPARK, close to Union Station

faq.question: Is the St. Louis Marathon hilly?
faq.answer: It is rolling. Race listings call it largely flat with some rolling hills, while a runner recap describes frequent hills in the middle and late miles. Listings disagree on the total climb, so no number is given here.

faq.question: When is the St. Louis Marathon held?
faq.answer: It is held in April, on a Saturday.

faq.question: Where does the St. Louis Marathon finish?
faq.answer: The official page places the finish festival outside CITYPARK, next to Union Station.
